newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles sharply higher with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles sharply higher with cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply higher Monday with western physical power prices because of heat seen smothering much of the western U.S. this week, market sources said.

Although mild weather conditions continued to hug the West Coast, a hot air system stretching from Montana down to New Mexico were predicted to push temperatures to as high as 100 degrees F across some interior areas into Thursday.
In addition to higher demand, limited amount of hydropower supply in the Northwest also propelled cash and futures values today, market sources said.
Water flow into regional hydroelectric systems in the Northwest and Canada has been slowed in recent days to refill reservoirs for fish migration requirements.
Many cash traders wanted to complete their power schedules for the rest of the week ahead of a two-day meeting called by the Western Systems Power Pool (WSPP), traders said.
The WSPP meeting to take place in Vancouver, Washington will begin Wednesday and end Thursday.
"They don't want to be caught short before going to the WSPP meeting," a Houston futures trader said.

Day-ahead firm peak power prices at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona jumped about $10.00 to $38.00-40.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), while those at the California-Oregon Border (COB) gained about five dollars to $25.00-26.00.
Some players also linked to the complex's strength to a technical rally in natural gas futures.
"It may have fueled the fire," the Houston trader said.
NYMEX September Henry Hub gas contract settled up 13.5 cents at $2.374 per million British thermal units after posting a new life-of-contract high at $2.385.
September PV futures settled up $2.36 at $31.04 a MWh, just 16 cents from the day's session high.
October PV finished up 87 cents at $23.17. Deferred PV contracts ended 25 to 60 cents higher.
September COB futures settled up $1.62 at $24.35 a MWh, trimming at $2.22 gain.
October COB finished up 91 cents at $22.14. Outer COB months ended up 20 to 45 cents.
Market sources said today's bullish momentum will likely continue into Tuesday.
"It looks like it's going to happen as long as cash stays strong," a West Coast broker said.
Separately, output from the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 3 in Wintersburg, Ariz., was reduced to 90 percent power as of early Monday for repairs to a condensate pump.
The unit was expected to return to full power within the next 48 hours, a spokesman for the plant said.
The adjacent 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear power unit 2 was operating at 93 percent of capacity as of early Monday as the unit coasts down to a scheduled refueling outage September 6.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected by Monday after being shut last week due to a rotor problem.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected by midnight Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
NYMEX estimated 273 COB and 642 PV contracts were sold.
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
